chart.title: Global primary energy use by source
chart.subtitle: Measured in terawatt-hours of total energy supply.
chart.note: Other renewables include geothermal, biomass, and waste. Traditional biomass is included but, in the absence of more recent data, it is assumed constant since 2015.
chart.citation: Energy Institute – Statistical Review of World Energy (2026); Smil (2017)

Traditional biomass.descriptionShort: Energy from traditional biomass (fuelwood, charcoal, crop residues, and dung), measured in terawatt-hours.
Traditional biomass.descriptionKey:
- Traditional biomass is fuelwood, charcoal, crop residues and dung. It is not part of total energy supply, which covers only fuels that are traded commercially.
- Traditional biomass is only available at the global level.
Traditional biomass.descriptionProcessing:
- Traditional biomass comes from Vaclav Smil's historical estimates (2017), which cover the World only, going back to 1800.
- Smil's estimates end in 2015. For later years, we assume that traditional biomass stays at its 2015 value.
Traditional biomass.citationShort: Smil (2017) – with major processing by Our World in Data
Traditional biomass.citationLong: Smil (2017) – with major processing by Our World in Data. “Traditional biomass” [dataset]. Smil, “Energy Transitions: Global and National Perspectives” [original data].
